n2-set-3-q-1.translation: More universities are incorporating volunteer activities into their elective courses.
n2-set-3-q-1.correctAnswerEnglish: 選択 (sentaku) - selection; an elective course

choices.reason: The second kanji 択 is read taku here, not daku; this voices the wrong syllable.
Both syllables are incorrectly voiced; 選択 begins with sen and ends with taku.
選択 is read sentaku; 選択科目 is an elective subject or course.
The ending taku is right, but 選 is sen, not zen, in 選択.

n2-set-3-q-2.translation: Constructing an airport requires an enormous amount of money.

choices.reason: 膨大 is read boudai and describes an enormous cost or quantity.
The first kanji 膨 is read bou in this word, not chou; choudai is not 膨大.
Bakudai is the reading of 莫大, another word for enormous, but the printed word is 膨大.
The first kanji is not read jin; 膨大 begins with bou.

n2-set-3-q-3.translation: A joke that I thought I had made lightly ended up hurting my friend.

choices.reason: 冗 is voiced as jou in 冗談, not shou.
The first syllable is long: jou, not short jo.
談 is read dan, with a voiced d, not tan.
冗談 is read joudan and means a joke or joking remark.

n2-set-3-q-4.translation: If the population keeps increasing like this, people around the world will probably end up fighting over food and water.
n2-set-3-q-4.correctAnswerEnglish: 奪い合い (ubaiai) - struggle or competition to take something from one another

choices.reason: Kisoi corresponds to 競い, meaning competition; the printed verb 奪う is read ubau.
奪い is ubai, from 奪う (ubau); 奪い合い means a struggle over a limited resource.
Arasoi means a dispute and is written 争い, not 奪い.
Ukagai comes from 伺う, to inquire or visit; it is not the reading of 奪い.

n2-set-3-q-5.translation: Recently, various efforts have been advancing to build apartments and homes with strong crime-prevention capabilities.
n2-set-3-q-5.correctAnswerEnglish: 性能 (seinou) - performance or functional capability

choices.reason: 性 is read sei in 性能, not zei.
Neither syllable matches the standard reading of 性能, seinou.
性 is not read suu here; 防犯性能 refers to security performance.
性能 is read seinou; 防犯性能 is the effectiveness of crime-prevention features.

n2-set-3-q-6.translation: That coach is good at bringing out the players' hidden abilities.

choices.reason: 隠れる means to be hidden; 隠れた能力 is a hidden ability.
陰 means shade or shadow, but 陰れた is not the standard spelling of kakureta.
隆 means flourishing or rising; 隆れた does not spell kakureta.
隔 means to separate; 隔れた is not the standard spelling of hidden.

n2-set-3-q-7.translation: Volcanic ash can enter electrical systems and cause various malfunctions.

choices.reason: 計 relates to counting or planning; 計統 is not the compound for an electrical system.
形 means shape; 形統 does not mean a system.
系統 means a system or line; 電気系統 is the electrical system.
経 means passing through or managing, but 経統 is not the spelling of keitou here.

n2-set-3-q-8.translation: From now on, buildings in cities will probably become increasingly high-rise.

choices.reason: 構想 means a plan or concept; 構想化 does not describe buildings growing taller.
高層 means high-rise; 高層化 means the shift toward taller buildings.
後送 means sending something back or to the rear, unrelated to building height.
効相 is not the compound for high-rise buildings; the intended kanji are 高層.

n2-set-3-q-9.translation: I think human beings are never freed from worrying throughout their lives.

choices.reason: 倣 means to imitate; 解倣 is not the word for being freed from worries.
封 means to seal; 解封 would refer to unsealing, not liberation from worries.
報 means report or reward; 解報 is not the word meaning release.
解放される means to be released or freed; 悩むことから解放されない means never being free of worry.

n2-set-3-q-10.translation: The nutritional value of vegetables and fruit has fallen compared with what it used to be.

choices.reason: 並べて means arranging side by side, not making a comparison of nutritional value.
比べて is the te-form of 比べる, to compare; 昔のものと比べて means compared with earlier produce.
列べて is not the standard spelling of kurabete for comparison.
対べて is not the standard spelling; 比 is the kanji used in 比べる.

n2-set-3-q-11.translation: Due to various circumstances, this event will be canceled.

choices.reason: 多 means many, but 多事情 is not the conventional compound in this notice.
複 means multiple or complex, but 複事情 is not the idiomatic expression.
重 means heavy or repeated, but 重事情 does not mean various circumstances.
諸 means various; 諸事情により is a standard formal phrase meaning due to various circumstances.

n2-set-3-q-12.translation: On Sunday, the family enjoyed a day trip.
n2-set-3-q-12.correctAnswerEnglish: 日帰り (higaeri) - a day trip, returning the same day

choices.reason: 日帰り means returning on the same day; 日帰りの旅行 is a day trip.
泊 means an overnight stay, so 泊帰り is not the day-trip compound.
行 relates to going, but 行帰り is not the set expression for a trip without an overnight stay.
出 means going out; 出帰り is not the standard compound here.

n2-set-3-q-13.translation: The road construction will begin in the next fiscal year.
n2-set-3-q-13.correctAnswerEnglish: 来年度 (rainendo) - next fiscal or school year

choices.reason: 未 means not yet, but 未年度 is not the word for next fiscal year.
来年度 means the coming fiscal or school year, matching when construction is to start.
数 means several or number; 数年度 is not the standard expression for next year.
真 means true or real; 真年度 is not a time expression.

n2-set-3-q-14.translation: A modern building equipped with the latest devices was constructed.

choices.reason: 風 means style, but 近代風な is not the expected adjective in this sentence.
式 denotes a type or ceremony; 近代式な is not the intended adjectival form.
The suffix 的 forms the na-adjective 近代的な, meaning modern.
性 means nature or tendency; 近代性な does not form the adjective used here.

n2-set-3-q-15.translation: I see promise in him because he often asks precise questions.
n2-set-3-q-15.correctAnswerEnglish: 将来性 (shouraisei) - future potential or promise

choices.reason: 将来感 is not the usual compound for a person's future potential.
将来性を感じる means to sense that someone has future potential.
化 indicates a process of change; 将来化 is not a word for promise.
風 means style or manner; 将来風 is not the expression here.

n2-set-3-q-16.translation: How did I do on the exam? It was not extremely good, but I think it was so-so.
n2-set-3-q-16.correctAnswerEnglish: まあまあ (maa maa) - so-so or reasonably good

choices.reason: せいぜい means at most; it does not serve as the predicate せいぜいだった for this moderate assessment.
そろそろ means soon or about time, not an assessment of exam performance.
ゆうゆう means easily or leisurely, inconsistent with the speaker's modest evaluation.
まあまあだった says the result was passable or fairly good, fitting 'not extremely good.'

n2-set-3-q-17.translation: If you compared her to an animal, her fickle side would make her rather catlike.
n2-set-3-q-17.correctAnswerEnglish: 例える (tatoeru) - compare or liken to

choices.reason: 動物に例える means to liken someone to an animal; it introduces the cat comparison.
比べる means to compare two things, usually AとBを比べる, not to liken a person to an animal with に.
たたえる means to praise or extol, not to make an analogy.
こたえる means to answer or respond, unrelated to the catlike description.

n2-set-3-q-18.translation: Because he acts on everything immediately, people mistakenly think he is an impatient person.
n2-set-3-q-18.correctAnswerEnglish: 誤解 (gokai) - misunderstanding or mistaking someone for something

choices.reason: 評判 is a reputation, but 評判されている is not the natural construction for being mistakenly regarded as impatient.
結論 means conclusion; 結論されている is not how one says people misjudge him.
気が短い人間だと誤解されている means he is misunderstood as being short-tempered.
決定 means decision; his personality is not being formally decided by others.

n2-set-3-q-19.translation: In the past, poor people who were not aristocrats lived in small, humble houses.

choices.reason: 不利 means disadvantageous, not a description of the physical condition of a house.
不幸 means unhappy or unfortunate; it does not naturally modify 家 as a house's quality.
地味 means plain or subdued, but the poor, small dwellings are described as 粗末, humble or shabby.
粗末な家 is a shabby or humble home, consistent with poverty in the sentence.

n2-set-3-q-20.translation: New employees are full of fresh appeal.
n2-set-3-q-20.correctAnswerEnglish: フレッシュ (furesshu) - fresh or youthful

choices.reason: オープン means open, but オープンな魅力 is not the intended description of new employees' fresh appeal.
フレッシュな魅力 expresses the youthful, new appeal associated with new employees.
ダイレクト means direct; ダイレクトな魅力 does not convey the newness emphasized by 新入社員.
ショック means a shock and does not form the natural description ショックな魅力.

n2-set-3-q-21.translation: These sneakers combine ease of walking with a good design.
n2-set-3-q-21.correctAnswerEnglish: 兼ね備えている (kanesonaete iru) - possess both qualities

choices.reason: 持ち備える is not the idiomatic compound for having two qualities at once.
造り備える is not a natural verb; 造る concerns making or building.
取り備える is not the set compound for combining qualities.
兼ね備える means to possess both; here the shoes have comfort and good design.

n2-set-3-q-22.translation: Everything needed for daily life is available in this shopping district.
n2-set-3-q-22.correctAnswerEnglish: 生活必需品 (seikatsu hitsujuhin) - daily necessities

choices.reason: 季節品 would mean seasonal goods, not all essentials for everyday living.
生活必需品 is the fixed compound for items necessary in daily life.
付属品 are accessories or attachments, not everyday necessities.
消耗品 are consumables; the sentence refers more broadly to daily necessities.

n2-set-3-q-23.translation: My older sister indiscriminately buys even things she does not need.
n2-set-3-q-23.correctAnswerEnglish: 考えなしに (kangae nashi ni) - without thinking or indiscriminately

choices.reason: やたらに means recklessly or indiscriminately, so 'without thinking' fits buying unnecessary things.
思いっきり means with all one's might or to one's heart's content, not necessarily without judgment.
絶えず means continually; frequency alone does not express やたらに's lack of restraint.
大量に means in large quantities; quantity is not the same as indiscriminate buying.

n2-set-3-q-24.translation: She is a person who never lets her guard down.
n2-set-3-q-24.correctAnswerEnglish: 油断 (yudan) - carelessness or letting one's guard down

choices.reason: 余裕 means room or composure; 隙がない here means no vulnerable opening, not no spare capacity.
夢 means dream, unrelated to 隙, an opening or lapse.
隙のない describes someone who leaves no opening; 油断 is the lapse or carelessness such a person avoids.
特徴 means characteristic; it does not convey an unguarded opening.

n2-set-3-q-25.translation: They are proceeding carefully with drafting a new bill.
n2-set-3-q-25.correctAnswerEnglish: 注意深く (chuui bukaku) - carefully or attentively

choices.reason: 容易に means easily, not with caution.
計画的に means systematically or according to a plan; that is not the same as 慎重に, cautiously.
注意深く means attentively and carefully, matching 慎重に when preparing a bill.
素早く means quickly, which says nothing about carefulness.

n2-set-3-q-26.translation: The president of the company that caused the accident was criticized by the media.
n2-set-3-q-26.correctAnswerEnglish: 非難された (hinan sareta) - was criticized or condemned

choices.reason: 質問された means was questioned; 叩かれた here implies hostile criticism, not merely questions.
称賛された means was praised, the opposite of the negative media response.
注目された means attracted attention; 叩かれた is specifically critical attention.
In this media context, 叩かれた figuratively means was attacked or condemned in public.

n2-set-3-q-27.translation: This guitar is a rare, limited-production item.
n2-set-3-q-27.correctAnswerEnglish: めずらしい (mezurashii) - rare or unusual

choices.reason: 新しい means new; a limited-production item can be rare without being new.
レア means rare; limited production explains why this guitar is unusual.
高い means expensive; rarity does not by itself state the price.
すばらしい means excellent; the sentence emphasizes scarcity, not quality.

n2-set-3-q-28.translation: This festival expresses gratitude for receiving the blessings of nature.
n2-set-3-q-28.correctAnswerEnglish: 恩恵 (onkei) - benefit or blessing bestowed on someone

choices.reason: 自然の恩恵に浴する means to enjoy or receive nature's benefits; this is the appropriate use of 恩恵.
Returning a personal favor is 恩返し, not 恩恵返し; 恩恵 names a benefit received.
A shrine amulet may have ご利益, a blessing or efficacy, but 恩恵がある is not the intended amulet expression.
For being able to graduate thanks to a teacher, おかげで is natural; 先生の恩恵で is not the intended usage here.

n2-set-3-q-29.translation: This is a dish that an amateur could never make.

choices.reason: The intended group affected by higher taxes is ordinary people, not necessarily amateurs; 素人 contrasts with experts.
素人には作れない contrasts an amateur's skills with those required for this dish.
For an unknown man as a marriage prospect, どこの誰だかわからない fits; 素人 describes expertise, not identity.
Being very beautiful is not a consequence of being 素人, an amateur; the causal だけあって is misplaced.

n2-set-3-q-30.translation: What a spineless person to get discouraged by something like that.
n2-set-3-q-30.correctAnswerEnglish: だらしない (darashinai) - spineless, sloppy or undisciplined

choices.reason: A poor job of helping with housework would be いい加減 or 雑; だらしない alone does not describe the work naturally here.
For work that is too dull to continue, つまらなくて fits; だらしない describes conduct or self-discipline.
だらしない can criticize lack of resolve; giving up over something minor makes the person seem spineless.
Keeping careful household accounts indicates discipline with money, the opposite of お金にだらしない.

n2-set-3-q-31.translation: Even now, many schools in Japan place more emphasis on reading than on speaking.
n2-set-3-q-31.correctAnswerEnglish: 重点を置く (juuten o oku) - place emphasis on

choices.reason: 重点を置く is the fixed expression for placing emphasis on something, here reading study.
The key to a plan's success is 鍵 or 重要な点, not 成功の重点.
An influential figure in business is 重鎮, not 重点; 重点 means emphasis or focus.
Words may have weight or substance, 重み, but 重点のある言葉 is not the intended expression.

n2-set-3-q-32.translation: At this company, family allowances are paid in addition to salary.
n2-set-3-q-32.correctAnswerEnglish: 支給される (shikyuu sareru) - be provided or paid out

choices.reason: A qualification is granted or awarded, 資格を与える, rather than 支給する, which supplies money or goods.
A customer pays a shopkeeper, 支払う; 支給する is not used for a retail payment.
A passport is issued, 旅券の発給, not 支給; the latter is for funds or supplies.
Family allowances are monetary benefits a company pays out; 手当が支給される is natural.

n2-set-3-q-33.translation: Now that I have accepted the job, I must finish it no matter what happens.
n2-set-3-q-33.correctAnswerEnglish: 上は (ue wa) - now that; since one has committed to doing it

choices.reason: 上から means from above or from the point of view of; it does not express the obligation following acceptance.
上で after a past verb means after doing something; it does not itself convey the resolve 'now that I have accepted it.'
上に means in addition to; the second clause is not an added fact about accepting the job.
Verb-past plus 上は means now that a decision is made; it naturally leads to the firm obligation 完成させなければならない.

n2-set-3-q-34.translation: I forgot my wallet, but thanks to having a credit card, I managed to shop anyway.
n2-set-3-q-34.correctAnswerEnglish: おかげで (okage de) - thanks to; because of a favorable cause

choices.reason: せいで blames a cause for a bad result, but being able to shop is a favorable result.
くせに means despite or even though, often with reproach; it does not credit the card for helping.
ものの means although; it marks contrast, not the helpful cause of being able to shop.
持っていたおかげで identifies the credit card as the reason the speaker could still make purchases.

n2-set-3-q-35.translation: Knowing how stingy she is, she would never buy a real diamond.
n2-set-3-q-35.correctAnswerEnglish: のことだから (no koto dakara) - knowing that person's character

choices.reason: のことから is not the pattern used to predict someone's behavior from a known personality trait.
彼女のことだから uses her known stinginess to infer that she would not buy a real diamond.
のこととはいえ means even though it concerns that person; it does not make the character-based inference.
のことにしては is not the grammatical pattern for this prediction; にしては usually marks an unexpected contrast.

n2-set-3-q-36.translation: Company A is a rival, but depending on the terms, we could negotiate a merger.
n2-set-3-q-36.correctAnswerEnglish: 次第では (shidai de wa) - depending on the conditions

choices.reason: 以前では means before, not depending on the proposed merger terms.
条件次第では means if the conditions allow it; this determines whether merger talks are possible.
程度では means at that degree or level; it does not express a conditional decision based on terms.
事情では refers to circumstances but is not the fixed pattern 条件次第では.

n2-set-3-q-37.translation: In preparation for a major earthquake, let's check the route home on a map.
n2-set-3-q-37.correctAnswerEnglish: に備えて (ni sonaete) - in preparation for

choices.reason: に応じて means in response to or according to; the quake has not happened yet.
に向かって means toward; checking a map is not movement toward an earthquake.
大地震に備えて means preparing for a possible major earthquake in advance.
に関して means concerning; it does not express the purpose of advance preparation.

n2-set-3-q-38.translation: In Japan, cherry blossoms are so central to spring that even their blooming makes the news; you cannot talk about spring without them.
n2-set-3-q-38.correctAnswerEnglish: ぬきには (nuki ni wa) - without; not apart from

choices.reason: だけでは means with only; さくらだけでは語れない would say blossoms alone are insufficient, the opposite emphasis.
さくらぬきには語れない means spring cannot be discussed without mentioning cherry blossoms.
ほどには means not to the extent of; it does not form the 'cannot do without' pattern.
のみでは means with only; like だけでは, it does not say blossoms are indispensable.

n2-set-3-q-39.translation: Caller: Hello, is President Yamashita available? Staff member: He is away from his desk at the moment, so I will have him call you back.
n2-set-3-q-39.correctAnswerEnglish: 席をはずしておりますので (seki o hazushite orimasu node) - he is away from his desk, so...

choices.reason: はずされております is passive, as though someone removed him from the seat; the idiom is 席をはずす.
はずしていらっしゃいます uses honorific language for one's own company president to an outside caller; the printed explanation requires humble language.
席をはずしております is the polite, humble form used by company staff when speaking to an outside caller about their own president.
はずしてしまいます suggests he will leave or has unfortunately left, not that he is currently away from his desk.

n2-set-3-q-40.translation: I am writing the paper in a hurry, but at this rate it does not look as though I will meet the deadline.
n2-set-3-q-40.correctAnswerEnglish: 間に合いそうもない (maniai sou mo nai) - unlikely to make it in time

choices.reason: The masu-stem plus そうもない expresses that meeting the deadline appears very unlikely.
間に合わないはずがない means there is no way I will fail to make it, contrary to このままでは.
間に合うわけでもない only says it is not necessarily true that I will make it; it misses the strong negative outlook.
間に合うほかない means there is no alternative but to make it, not that success looks unlikely.

n2-set-3-q-41.translation: Just because I did not know the rules here, I caused everyone trouble.
n2-set-3-q-41.correctAnswerEnglish: 知らなかったばかりに (shiranakatta bakari ni) - solely because I did not know

choices.reason: 知っていただけに means precisely because I knew, usually followed by a contrast; the speaker did not know the rules.
知らなかっただけに means all the more because I did not know; the printed causal pattern for the bad outcome is ばかりに.
知っていたばかりに blames knowing the rules, contradicting the intended cause.
ばかりに marks a cause that produced an undesirable outcome: the speaker's ignorance inconvenienced others.

n2-set-3-q-42.translation: Unless you speak up, there should be no one who knows about this.
n2-set-3-q-42.correctAnswerEnglish: 人はいないはずだ (hito wa inai hazu da) - there should be no one

choices.reason: 人がいるはずだ says somebody must know, opposite to the condition 'unless you speak.'
しゃべらない限り means unless you speak; with no other source of disclosure, no one should know.
人がいるということだ asserts that someone knows, contrary to the conditional secrecy.
人がいないということだ reports a conclusion as fact; はずだ expresses the expected result of the condition more naturally.

n2-set-3-q-43.translation: Food is not necessarily tastier the fresher it is; some foods taste better when they are a little older.
n2-set-3-q-43.correctAnswerEnglish: おいしいわけではなく (oishii wake de wa naku) - it is not necessarily tasty

choices.reason: おいしいはずで says it should be tasty, leaving no room for the contrast that some older foods taste better.
わけではない gives a partial negation: freshness does not always guarantee better taste.
おいしくないはずで predicts fresher food should not taste good, opposite to the usual expectation in the first clause.
おいしくないわけではなく says it is not necessarily bad, which does not directly negate 'fresher is tastier.'

n2-set-3-q-44.translation: In modern Japan, being the eldest son does not necessarily mean that you will take over the family line or business.
n2-set-3-q-44.correctAnswerEnglish: つぐわけではない (tsugu wake de wa nai) - does not necessarily inherit or succeed

choices.reason: だからといって with わけではない rejects the claim that every eldest son must succeed the family.
つがないではいられない says one cannot help succeeding, which would imply compulsion.
ついではならない means must not take over, a prohibition not stated in the sentence.
つがざるを得ない means have no choice but to succeed, the opposite of the partial negation.

n2-set-3-q-45.translation: If you are having trouble, I would like to help you, for my part, but...
n2-set-3-q-45.correctAnswerEnglish: しては (shite wa) - as for, in the phrase 私としては at the marked third blank

choices.reason: 助けて (tasukete) connects to あげたい, 'want to help you'; it is the fourth fragment, not the starred third one.
The complete order is いるなら, 私と, しては, 助けて. 私としては means 'as far as I am concerned'; しては fills the starred third blank.
いるなら (iru nara) completes 困っているなら, 'if you are in trouble'; it belongs first.
私と (watashi to) begins 私としては and follows 困っているなら; it belongs second, immediately before the star.

n2-set-3-q-46.translation: My wife saves even ten yen on the one hand, yet sometimes buys expensive clothes without a second thought.
n2-set-3-q-46.correctAnswerEnglish: 一方で (ippou de) - while, on the other hand, at the marked third blank

choices.reason: 平気 (heiki) combines with the printed で to make 平気で, 'without hesitation'; it is the fourth fragment.
10円を (juu-en o) is the object of 節約する, 'save ten yen'; it is the first fragment.
The complete order is 10円を, 節約する, 一方で, 平気. 節約する一方で contrasts her thrift with expensive shopping; 一方で is the starred third fragment.
節約する (setsuyaku suru) completes 10円を節約する and stands before 一方で, in the second blank.

n2-set-3-q-47.translation: Because this shop's cakes are not too sweet, they are popular with men as well as women.
n2-set-3-q-47.correctAnswerEnglish: もちろん (mochiron) - of course; part of 'not only women but also men' at the star

choices.reason: The order is 甘すぎないので, 女性は, もちろん, 男性に. 女性はもちろん男性にも means 'not only with women but with men too'; もちろん is the third, starred fragment.
甘すぎないので (amasuginai node) gives the reason the cakes appeal broadly; it belongs first.
女性は (josei wa) begins the paired phrase 女性はもちろん男性にも, so it is second, before the star.
男性に (dansei ni) takes the printed も to make 男性にも, 'also among men'; it is fourth.

n2-set-3-q-48.translation: Knowing how careless Yamashita is about time, he is probably slacking off somewhere again.
n2-set-3-q-48.correctAnswerEnglish: だから (dakara) - because of; completing 山下さんのことだから at the star

choices.reason: こと (koto) completes 山下さんのこと, 'knowing Yamashita'; it is the first fragment.
また (mata) means again and modifies the suspected repeated slacking; it belongs after だから, in the third blank overall after the star.
どこか (dokoka) means somewhere and combines with the printed で, forming どこかで; it is last.
The complete order is こと, だから, また, どこか. 山下さんのことだから draws an inference from his known habit; だから is the starred second blank.

n2-set-3-q-49.translation: When I followed the flow of people walking, the event venue was farther ahead.
n2-set-3-q-49.correctAnswerEnglish: 沿って (sotte) - following or along; the starred third fragment

choices.reason: 流れに (nagare ni) means 'to/along the flow' and follows 人の歩く; it is second, not starred.
進むと (susumu to) means 'when I went forward' and follows 沿って; it is the fourth fragment.
The complete order is 歩く, 流れに, 沿って, 進むと. 人の歩く流れに沿って進むと means 'when I went along the flow of people walking'; 沿って is starred.
歩く (aruku) modifies 流れ, forming 'the flow of people walking'; it belongs first.

n2-set-3-q-50.translation: Single-mother households receive a child-rearing allowance according to their income, along with other forms of support.
n2-set-3-q-50.correctAnswerEnglish: に応じた (ni oujita) - according to or corresponding to income

choices.reason: に伴った (ni tomonatta) means accompanying a change or event; the allowance amount is tied to the income level.
収入に応じた means adjusted according to income; it modifies the child-rearing allowance paid to single-mother households.
に比べた (ni kurabeta) means compared with; no second income is being compared in this clause.
に沿った (ni sotta) means in line with a policy or path, not calibrated to household income.

n2-set-3-q-51.translation: Because the traditional view expected husbands to earn money and wives to manage the home and children, single-mother households often struggled financially. By contrast, people assumed single-father households had no financial problems compared with single-mother households.
n2-set-3-q-51.correctAnswerEnglish: a 母子家庭 / b 母子家庭 / c 父子家庭 (boshi katei / boshi katei / fushi katei) - single-mother, single-mother, single-father households

choices.reason: Putting 父子家庭 at a reverses the passage's claim: it was single-mother households thought to face financial difficulty. Putting 母子家庭 at c reverses the comparison too.
a must be 母子家庭, because the preceding traditional division of labor explains mothers' lost earnings; this option wrongly places fathers at a and mothers at c.

choices.romaji: boshi katei / boshi katei / fushi katei
choices.reason: a is single-mother households, formerly seen as needing aid. b is the same comparison group; c is single-father households, formerly assumed financially secure.
Although a is correctly single-mother households, b and c are reversed: the sentence compares single-father households with single-mother households, not with themselves.

n2-set-3-q-52.translation: However, although the income of single-father households is not as low as that of single-mother households, it was found to be far below the overall average.
n2-set-3-q-52.correctAnswerEnglish: 低くはないものの (hikuku wa nai mono no) - although it is not as low

choices.reason: 低いにしても means even if it is low; the passage instead says fathers' income is not as low as mothers', but still below average.
低いはずがなく means it cannot possibly be low; the passage reports that it is substantially below average.
低くはないものの concedes that single-father income is not as low as single-mother income, then contrasts it with the much lower-than-average figure.
低いと思ったら means when one thought it was low; this does not set up the intended concession before the comparison with the average.

n2-set-3-q-53.translation: This is because long overtime and weekend work are taken for granted for men in Japan, and few companies will employ a man who must leave at five to collect his child from daycare.
n2-set-3-q-53.correctAnswerEnglish: というのも (to iu no mo) - this is because

choices.reason: This introduces the explanation for the preceding finding that single-father households earn less than average: workplace expectations make caregiving difficult.
だからといって means even so or just because of that; the following sentences explain the cause rather than qualify it.
にもかかわらず means despite, which would contradict the causal link between long work hours and lower earnings.
とはいえ means nevertheless or that said; the passage needs an explanatory connector, not another concession.

n2-set-3-q-54.translation: Even men who are already employed may have to switch from full-time positions to part-time work; men, too, can therefore end up on low incomes. The government accordingly decided to extend child-rearing allowances to low-income single-father households.
n2-set-3-q-54.correctAnswerEnglish: 低収入になり得るのです (teishuunyuu ni nari uru no desu) - can end up with a low income

choices.reason: 高収入になりかねません means may end up with a high income, which conflicts with the problem of low-income single fathers.
高収入にならざるを得ません means have no choice but to earn a high income, the opposite of the described economic difficulty.
低収入になり得ないのです means cannot become low-income, contradicting the finding that some single-father households need support.

choices.romaji: teishuunyuu ni nari uru no desu
choices.reason: なり得る expresses real possibility: childcare constraints can leave men on low incomes, motivating the extension of benefits.
